facts: Chicago is famous for its striking architecture, including the Willis Tower, once the world's tallest building.
The Chicago Marathon is one of the six prestigious World Marathon Majors, attracting thousands of runners annually.
Nestled along Lake Michigan, Chicago features a continuous twenty-six-mile lakefront trail perfect for scenic long runs.
Chicago was incorporated as a city in 1837 and quickly grew into a major transportation hub.
The famous Bean sculpture, officially named Cloud Gate, sits in Millennium Park and reflects the city's skyline.
Deep-dish pizza, with its thick crust and rich layers of cheese and tomato sauce, originated right here in Chicago.
Chicago is nicknamed the Windy City, a moniker originally popularized by rival city journalists in the nineteenth century.
The Chicago River is famous for being dyed bright green every year to celebrate Saint Patrick's Day.
Sue, the most complete Tyrannosaurus rex fossil ever discovered, resides at Chicago's Field Museum.
Legendary basketball player Michael Jordan led the Chicago Bulls to six NBA championships during the 1990s.
Chicago's Lincoln Park Zoo is one of the oldest free public zoos in the United States.
Jazz and blues music flourished in Chicago, shaping modern American musical traditions for generations.
The historic Route 66 highway officially begins right in downtown Chicago at Adams Street.
Navy Pier extends over three thousand feet into Lake Michigan, offering iconic views and entertainment.
Kelvin Kiptum set the men's marathon world record right here on the streets of Chicago in 2023.
Chicago features more than six hundred parks, making it a fantastic city for urban runners to explore.
The iconic Chicago hot dog is always served on a poppy seed bun and never includes ketchup.
Wrigley Field, home of the Chicago Cubs, is one of the oldest and most beloved baseball parks in America.
Chicago engineers famously reversed the flow of the Chicago River in 1900 for sanitation purposes.
Nobel Peace Prize winner Jane Addams founded Hull House in Chicago to aid newly arrived European immigrants.
